# RFC 5531 reference audit results
## Audit scope
Every `RFC 5531 §X` (and `RFC 5531 Appendix X`) citation in the repository was located via `grep -rn "RFC 5531\|RFC5531\|rfc5531\|rfc 5531"` across `Sources/`, `Tests/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, and `README.ko.md`, then cross-checked against the actual table of contents and section bodies of `docs/rfc5531.txt`.
For reference, the real top-level structure of RFC 5531 is:
- §1 Introduction - §2 Changes since RFC 1831 - §3 Terminology - §4 The RPC Model - §5 Transports and Semantics - §6 Binding and Rendezvous Independence - §7 Authentication - §8 RPC Protocol Requirements - §8.1 RPC Programs and Procedures - §8.2 Authentication, Integrity, and Privacy - §8.3 Program Number Assignment - §8.4 Other Uses of the RPC Protocol - §9 The RPC Message Protocol (defines `rpc_msg`, `msg_type`, `reply_stat`, `accept_stat`, `reject_stat`, `auth_stat`, `call_body`, `accepted_reply`, `rejected_reply`, `mismatch_info`, plus the `xid` matching rule) - §10 Authentication Protocols - §11 Record Marking Standard - §12 The RPC Language - §13 IANA Considerations - §14 Security Considerations - Appendix A System Authentication (defines `authsys_parms` for AUTH_SYS, plus the rules for the AUTH_SYS reply verifier flavor) - Appendix B Requesting RPC-Related Numbers from IANA - Appendix C Current Number Assignments
Notable: **Appendix A has no sub-numbering**. There is no `Appendix A.1`, `Appendix A.2`, or `§A.2` in RFC 5531.
## Hallucinations identified and corrected
### `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCMessage.swift:24`
- The cited `RFC 5531 Appendix A.1` for the AUTH_SYS credential body (`authsys_parms`) does not exist — Appendix A is a flat appendix with no sub-numbering. - The `authsys_parms` struct itself is in fact defined in **Appendix A** (System Authentication), so the citation was corrected to `RFC 5531 Appendix A`.
### `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCMessage.swift:152`
- The comment "the verifier is AUTH_NONE, which is what AUTH_SYS expects for replies (RFC 5531 §8.2)" pinned the AUTH_SYS-specific reply-verifier rule to §8.2. - §8.2 (Authentication, Integrity, and Privacy) only defines the generic `opaque_auth` envelope and the `auth_flavor` enum; it does not say anything about *which* flavor an AUTH_SYS reply verifier should carry. - The actual normative statement — "The flavor value of the verifier received in the reply message from the server may be 'AUTH_NONE' or 'AUTH_SHORT'" — lives in **Appendix A**. The citation was corrected to `RFC 5531 Appendix A` accordingly.
### `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCConstants.swift:36`
- The `RPCAuthStatus` enum was annotated as `RFC 5531 §A.2 — auth_stat`. - Two problems: (a) `§A.2` (or `Appendix A.2`) does not exist in RFC 5531 at all, and (b) the `auth_stat` enum is not in Appendix A in any form — it is defined in **§9** (The RPC Message Protocol), as part of the same block that defines `accept_stat` and `reject_stat`. - Citation corrected to `RFC 5531 §9 — auth_stat`, which makes this enum's section reference consistent with the neighboring `RPCAcceptStatus` (`§9 — accept_stat`) and `RPCRejectStatus` (`§9 — reject_stat`) annotations in the same file.
## Citations verified as correct (left unchanged)
- `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCRecordMarking.swift:4` — `§11` for record marking - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCRecordMarking.swift:39` — `§11` for the streaming decoder - `Sources/NanoNFS/XDR/XDR.swift:15` — `§11` for oversize-fragment guards - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCMessage.swift:4` — `§9` for `rpc_msg` - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCMessage.swift:14` — `§8.2` for `opaque_auth` (≤400 byte body) - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCMessage.swift:20` — `§8.2` for `opaque_auth.body` length cap - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCMessage.swift:145` — `§11` for the record-mark header - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCConstants.swift:6` — `§9` for `rpc_msg.rpcvers == 2` - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCConstants.swift:20` — `§9` for `accept_stat` - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCConstants.swift:30` — `§9` for `reject_stat` - `Sources/NanoNFS/RPC/RPCConstants.swift:50` — `§8.2` for `auth_flavor` - `Sources/NanoNFS/Wire/RPCSession.swift:37` — `§9` for program identification (`prog`/`vers`/`proc` in `call_body`) - `Sources/NanoNFS/Public/NFSServerListener.swift:119` — `§9` for the xid-matching rule - `Tests/NanoNFSTests/ListenerIntegrationTests.swift:165` — `§9` for the xid-matching rule - `Tests/NanoNFSTests/RPCTests.swift:6` — bare `RFC 5531`, no specific section - `README.md:59` / `README.ko.md:59` — bare `RFC 5531`, no specific section - `CLAUDE.md:42 / 162 / 166` — bare `RFC 5531`, no specific section - `CLAUDE.md:266` — `§9` for the xid-matching rule
## Build status
`swift build` succeeds after the edits. No code semantics changed — the corrections are purely in doc-comments.
agent-task-report.note:
# Audit method note
- The audit was driven entirely by `grep` over the working tree plus direct reads of `docs/rfc5531.txt`. No memory-based reasoning about RFC 5531 section numbers was used (per `CLAUDE.md` §4 anti-hallucination rule), since this audit is itself the meta-version of that rule applied to RFC 5531. - The pattern of the three found defects is the same one that showed up in the 2026-05-09 RFC 7530 audit: appendix sub-numbering invented out of thin air (`Appendix A.1`, `§A.2`) and a section pinned to the closest-feeling chapter rather than the one that actually defines the cited concept (§8.2 vs Appendix A for AUTH_SYS reply-verifier rules). Worth keeping in mind for future RFC reference passes.
